title: Tesla: Electrical Genius
description: Electrical wizardry, fierce rivalry, and wireless dreams—five inventor depths.

questions.question: What kind of electricity, which reverses direction many times a second, did Tesla champion as the standard for power grids?
questions.hint: It's abbreviated as AC and changes direction periodically
questions.explanation: In July 1888 George Westinghouse licensed Tesla's AC motor patents for cash, stock and a royalty per horsepower—then bet his company on them against a famous foe.

questions.question: Tesla's alternating current drew a fierce rival—which inventor championed direct current in the War of Currents?
questions.hint: He invented the light bulb and preferred direct current (DC)
questions.explanation: Tesla had briefly worked for Edison's company in 1884. In the war, Edison's camp aided Harold Brown, who electrocuted animals in public demonstrations to brand AC as deadly.

questions.question: Edison's DC rival Tesla discovered what principle that made practical AC motors possible?
questions.hint: It involves magnetic fields that spin around in a circle
questions.explanation: By Tesla's own account, it hit him in 1882 in a Budapest park as he recited Goethe's Faust at sunset—and he sketched the motor in the sand with a stick.

questions.question: After the rotating magnetic field made AC motors practical, Tesla chased wireless power at a high-altitude lab in what Rocky Mountain city?
questions.hint: A mountainous state's springs-named city where he created artificial lightning
questions.explanation: There in 1899 he made man-made lightning and heard rhythmic signals he later insisted came from Mars. Historians suspect Marconi's experiments or natural radio noise.

questions.question: From Colorado Springs, Tesla moved east to build what unfinished Long Island wireless tower?
questions.hint: Named after the benefactor James S. Warden, it was meant to transmit power wirelessly across the Atlantic
questions.explanation: J.P. Morgan put in $150,000, but the money ran out and the tower was scrapped in 1917 to pay debts. In 2012, The Oatmeal's Matthew Inman crowdfunded $1.37M to save the site.

deeperMode.description: Obsessive habits and visions ahead of their time

questions.question: Tesla had an obsessive fear of this round object and refused to touch jewelry containing them.
questions.hint: Formed inside oysters, these smooth spherical gems disturbed his sense of symmetry

questions.question: What did Tesla call his theoretical wireless communication device that predicted modern smartphones?
questions.hint: He envisioned a global network where people could communicate instantly anywhere
